# Hermes Agent FAQ & Troubleshooting Guide

## 1. Getting Started, UI & Observability
- **Web Dashboard:** Run `hermes dashboard` to launch the local browser UI on `http://127.0.0.1:9119` with an embedded chat terminal.
- **Observability & Tracing:** Langfuse is bundled as an opt-in plugin. Enable it with `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse` (or via `hermes tools`) to trace tool call chains and inspect input/output arguments.
- **Security Vulnerabilities:** Follow `SECURITY.md`. Report vulnerabilities confidentially via [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) or email `security@nousresearch.com`.

---

## 2. Model Providers & Authentication
- **Local Ollama Overridden by Remote Keys:** If local requests fail with remote HTTP 401 errors, Hermes is auto-detecting environment keys (e.g., Anthropic). Set `provider: custom` alongside your `base_url` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` to disable auto-routing.
- **Ollama Cloud 404s:** Ollama Cloud uses OpenAI-compatible `/v1` endpoints (`https://ollama.com/v1`). Set `provider: ollama-cloud` in your configuration.
- **Small Local Models (4B–9B) Run Slowly:** Hermes sends the complete tool schema (~45 tools) on each turn. To improve latency:
  1. Disable unused toolsets with `hermes tools`.
  2. Use faster quantization or larger models (32B+).
  3. Set `terminal.backend: local` to eliminate container overhead.
- **Custom / Local Vision:** Enable native image payloads for Ollama/custom models by setting `supports_vision: true` in your model configuration.
- **Azure AI Foundry:** Run `hermes setup` or specify `provider: azure-foundry` (auto-detects `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL`). Claude Code-specific env vars (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY`, etc.) are ignored.
- **Claude Pro/Max vs. API Billing:** Anthropic API keys always incur per-token API charges. To use your Pro/Max subscription allowance, authenticate via OAuth.
- **Google Gemini:** Legacy CLI OAuth is deprecated. Authenticate using `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY` via Google AI Studio.
- **DeepSeek V4 Model Aliasing:** In older versions, `deepseek-v4-flash` was normalized to `deepseek-chat`. Update to the latest release to ensure flash models pass through without pro-tier billing.
- **Token Usage on LocalAI / OpenAI-Compatible Backends:** Streaming requests automatically include `stream_options: {include_usage: true}` so `/usage` correctly tracks token metrics.

---

## 3. Context, Memory & Personas
- **Agent Identity & Memory Files:**
  - `SOUL.md`: Base agent persona, tone, and system-level instructions.
  - `USER.md`: Persistent user identity, background, and preferences (`target="user"`).
  - `MEMORY.md`: Long-term episodic memory and recalled facts.
- **Turn Limits & Autonomous Tasks:** Controlled per-session by `agent.max_turns` (default: 90; CLI override: `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`). For long-running, multi-step tasks across sessions, use `/goal` and resume paused tasks with `/goal resume`.
- **Context Compaction:** `ContextCompressor` automatically prunes and deduplicates stale tool outputs. Pluggable alternatives can be configured under `context.engine`.
- **Skill Tracking:** View loaded skills and execution statistics with `/insights` or `hermes insights` (logged in `~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json`).

---

## 4. Gateway & Messaging Integrations
- **Interactive Setup:** Configure chat platforms step-by-step using `hermes gateway setup`.
- **Telegram "Unauthorized User" Fix:** `allowed_chats` only filters group IDs. For direct messages, authorize users via:
  - Adding user IDs to `telegram.allow_from` in `config.yaml`.
  - Direct messaging the bot and approving the code on the host: `hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>`.
  - Setting `telegram.allow_all: true` (open access).
- **Per-Channel Personas:** Define distinct prompts per channel or group across Discord, Telegram, Slack, and Mattermost via `channel_prompts`.
- **Multi-Profile Gateways:** Run multiple independent accounts (e.g., distinct WeChat/Telegram accounts) concurrently via profile multiplexing while keeping memory and configs isolated.
- **File & Media Routing:** Outbound documents dispatch to Matrix (`m.file`), Telegram, and Email (SMTP attachments). Remote images in DingTalk use Markdown `![image](url)` syntax. MCP image outputs (`MEDIA:<path>`) forward directly to supported channels.
- **Inbound Attachments:** Uploaded text and code files (`.py`, `.txt`) are automatically injected into the agent's context.
- **Session Continuity:** Sessions interrupted by restarts are preserved as `resume_pending`. Automated idle/daily resets default to off (`session_reset.mode: none`).

---

## 5. Extensibility & Development
- **Model Routing Policy:** Dynamic complexity-based routing (e.g., `smart_model_routing`) is not supported. Configure subagents via `delegation.provider` / `delegation.model` or switch models manually using `/model`.
- **Subagents:** Spawn parallel worker subagents using the `delegate_task` tool (default concurrency: up to 3).
- **Custom Tools:** Build personal tools as plugins in `~/.hermes/plugins/` and enable them via `hermes plugins enable <name>`. In-tree development requires defining tools in `tools/` and exposing them in `toolsets.py`.
- **Custom Memory Providers:** In-tree additions to `plugins/memory/` are closed. Distribute external backends as standalone plugins implementing the `MemoryProvider` ABC (`sync_turn`, `prefetch`, `shutdown`).

---

## 6. Installation & Platforms
- **Windows 10/11:** Native Tier 1 support via PowerShell installer (`install.ps1`). WSL2 is only needed if using the Dashboard POSIX PTY embedded terminal.
- **Docker / NAS Permissions:** When mounting host directories on Synology, unRAID, or UGOS Pro, pass `PUID` and `PGID` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`) to prevent `[Errno 13] Permission denied` errors on `/opt/data`. Official images support `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`.
- **Android (Termux):** Supported out-of-the-box via `scripts/install.sh` using the dedicated `.[termux-all]` package group.
- **Local Honcho:** Setting `base_url` to `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` automatically injects a placeholder API key.
- **Slow Updates:** Pauses during `hermes update` at the Node.js step are typically Camofox downloading browser binaries in the background.
